verdict: The anchor's core contrast (template-rendered coda correct, model-composed intro wrong) is real and verified at the code and at the live ledger, but three of its load-bearing citations are wrong or over-claimed, and it misses the one existing precedent that the operator's ruling is literally asking for: `_otr_line_composer.compose_news_coda` already ships a composite row (model bridge + Python-owned fact) structurally protected by `_otr_ledger_clean.PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG`. The bigger problem is the ruling's shape itself: public_domain `unit_label` is a curator's SCENE DESCRIPTOR on roughly half the corpus ("Harker at the castle", "Three wishes", "The meeting on the ice"), so a locator half rendered from it would make the deterministic, un-inventable half of the sentence invent a chapter on the invent-nothing lane — the exact failure `_otr_source_identity` was written to refuse. The verify idea on record cannot be built as stated; the residual check that IS worth building is a receipt check on Python's own rendered string surviving `ledger_clean`, not a prose check on whether the announcer named the work.

That constant did NOT run. `_otr_creative_prompt_router.resolve_creative_system_prompt` maps phase `announcer_intro_safe_system` through `_PHASE_TO_PACK_SEAM` into `_otr_story_pack.get_pack_prompt(resolve_story_pack(source_bank_id), seam)`, which RAISES rather than falling back (`get_pack_prompt`: 'RAISE if the seam is absent/empty. No fallback'). The constant survives only as the science-lane extraction fixture -- the router's own import comment says so. The seam actually sent on public_domain is `nodes/story_packs/public_domain/faithful_radio_adaptation.json` key `announcer_intro_safe_system`, which reads 'Sentence 1 names tonight's work from the WORK line ...' and 'Use ONLY the WORK title and the proper names in the cast list below; invent none.' The anchor's CONCLUSION survives and is strengthened (the real seam is more specific than the one quoted), but any r2 proposal aimed at the constant would edit dead text.

WRONG LEDGER SHAPE. The anchor writes `meta.announcer_intro_rewrite == "announcer_intro_rewritten"`. `OTR_LedgerScriptWriter` writes `meta.setdefault("announcer_intro_rewrite", {})["status"]` and `["reason"]` -- a DICT. Confirmed on the live artifact: `{'status': 'announcer_intro_rewritten', 'reason': None}`. A validator written literally from the anchor compares a dict to a str, never fires, and reports clean forever.

On THIS episode the scene-1 rows are 'I must insist upon immediate access to that file, Watson', 'Very well, Mr. Holmes', 'Ah, Watson!', 'Mr. Holmes, please.' -- so the announcer's prompt plausibly carried the strings Holmes/Watson. 'The Adventure of the Purloined Paper' is the Conan Doyle title template fused to a Poe title, which is a NAMED-ENTITY attractor route, not the 'bland real title loses to genre register' route the anchor asserts. The prompt is free of an excerpt and of `unit_label`; it is NOT free of laundered scene-1 material.

A SECOND FIDELITY DEFECT IN THE SAME ARTIFACT, UNNOTICED. The locked cast (ledger `cast` rows c02/c03) is `THE GREAT DETECTIVE` and `SECRETARY`, and `meta._adaptation_character_names` lists the Leacock roster. Lines b002-b005 nonetheless name 'Watson' and 'Mr. Holmes' -- Conan Doyle characters invented into a Leacock parody on the invent-nothing lane. The announcer title is downstream-consistent with that, which is evidence for the transcription route and is arguably the deeper root. The anchor treats the episode as having one defect.

THE CLOSEST PRECEDENT IS MISSED. The anchor points at `_otr_provenance` as 'the coda's winning mechanism', but the coda ROW is assembled in `_otr_line_composer._assemble_news_coda_surface` / `compose_news_coda`, which returns `LineResult(result, (flag, PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG))` precisely so a later model pass cannot delete the Python-owned span. Verified on the artifact: b006 carries `['news_coda_bridge', 'protected_fact_component']`. That composite-row-plus-protection pattern IS the operator's ruling, already shipped on the sibling surface, and the anchor's plan does not name it -- which is why it also does not notice hazard (4) below.

MINOR, SAME CALL SITE. The rewrite invokes `_OTRLC.compose_announcer_intro(... story_scaffold=True ...)`, but `compose_announcer_intro`'s signature absorbs unknown keywords into `**_compat` and never reads `story_scaffold`. The kwarg is dead. Not a cause of PBUG-04, but the anchor cites this call as evidence that 'item F changed both producers' without noticing the dead lever on it.
where_the_shape_breaks: THE LOCATOR HALF INVENTS ON HALF THE CORPUS -- this is the shape's biggest hole. Measured at `config/source_banks/public_domain_story/manifest.sample.json`: 65 units, 60 with `label != title`. `_otr_public_domain_sources.source_meta_from_unit` maps `unit_label = unit['label']` verbatim. Roughly half those labels are real piece titles ('The Quarter-Deck', 'The Speckled Band', 'Rikki-Tikki-Tavi', 'Marley's Ghost', 'The Ransom of Red Chief', 'Maddened by Mystery, or The Defective Detective') and roughly half are CURATOR SCENE DESCRIPTORS ('Harker at the castle', 'The meeting on the ice', 'Three wishes', 'The last night', 'The vaults', 'The first proposal', 'The interrupted wedding', 'The windmills', 'The air war', 'The cricket match', 'Anthony Rogers wakes in 2419', 'The Baron's tallest tales'). Rendering "Dracula, 'Harker at the castle'" announces a chapter Stoker never wrote -- an invention delivered by the half that is supposed to be un-inventable. `_otr_source_identity`'s module docstring already refuses to read `unit_label` for exactly this reason and states nothing distinguishes the two classes programmatically.

SHAKESPEARE'S `scene_label` IS NOT RENDERABLE. Verified at `config/source_banks/shakespeare/curated_scenes.sample.json`: every one of the 14 rows is a compound -- "Act 1, Scene 2 - Prospero opens the island's history", 'Act 1, Scene 3 - the prophecy on the heath'. Speaking it puts a curator's stage direction on air. The renderable fields are `act` and `scene`, which are INTS, so the operator's 'Act I Scene 2' also needs an int-to-roman step that exists nowhere in the repo. The anchor lists all four fields as 'locator data' without saying which is safe to speak.

THE TEMPLATE WOULD EMIT PUNCTUATION ITS OWN SEAM FORBIDS, AND TTS EATS SOME OF IT. `nodes/story_packs/public_domain/faithful_radio_adaptation.json` announcer_intro_safe_system says 'No speaker name, no colon, no quotation marks.' The ruling's shape ("Moby-Dick, 'The Quarter-Deck'") is a quoted span and a comma; the subtitle shape ('The Tempest: A Hot Take') is a colon. Separately `_otr_bark_lib` NFKD-normalizes then drops every non-ASCII character, so a curly quote or an accented title is silently mangled on the way to voice. The shipped defective row carries single quotes AND `unclean_spoken_text`.

`_otr_ledger_clean` CAN DELETE THE RENDERED NAME -- MUST-FIX. The intro rewrite (`_apply_intro_rewrite_result`) runs before `_run_writer_tail`'s `helper_context('ledger_clean')` block. The clean loop skips a row ONLY when `PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG in row['compose_flags']`. The shipped intro row carries `['announcer_intro', 'announcer_intro_rewritten', 'unclean_spoken_text']` -- it was judged and repair-attempted. So a template-rendered work title placed in that row sits inside a model's edit surface, and PBUG-20260815-01 (the LoC fact deleted on 9 of 14 voiced rows across three episodes) replays on the intro.

MEDIA_ARCHIVE: the lane gate is necessary but the FALLBACK branch reopens the hole. `identity_from_meta` puts the PUBLICATION in `work_title` for media_archive (`prov['work_title'] = 'meta.source_meta.source_label'`) and the headline in `post_headline`; the docstring measures 56 of 98 live ledgers carrying `source_label`. Any renderer reaching for `identity.work_title` without gating on `ADAPTATION_SOURCE_KINDS` announces 'a scene from Now See Hear!'. media_archive also has no `unit_label` and no `act`, so it would land on the subtitle branch, where nothing stops the same field being read. The `original` lane must keep `_work_line`'s empty-return behaviour that drops the WORK label entirely.

THE SUBTITLE BRANCH SPEAKS A KNOWN SCRATCH FIELD. The fallback reads `meta['episode_title']`, which PBUG-20260817-05 established is planted by harnesses: `scripts/otr_gpu_soak_matrix.py` now guards it (`HEADLESS_FORBIDDEN_TITLE_SOURCE = 'user'`, `title_receipt`, `leg_label` no longer passed as --title), but `scripts/otr_canonical_api_run.py` still maps `--title` onto the `episode_title` widget and `scripts/otr_macbeth_probe.py` still stamps `'episode_title': 'Macbeth II.ii safety probe'`. Today a planted label reaches the title card; under this ruling it would also be SPOKEN. The defective episode itself has `title_source = 'llm_post_composition'`, so it is clean -- the hazard is the next harness leg, not this one.

A NEW REQUIRED FIELD WOULD KILL RENDERS. `SafeOpenBrief.work_title` is documented 'OPTIONAL FOREVER: never required, never validated, never starves a brief', because adding it to `safe_open_viability` would raise `AnnouncerBriefStarvedError` before the creative call on every non-adaptation lane. A locator field must inherit that contract verbatim -- and note `safe_open_viability` is shared with `_otr_story_brief._validate_produced_open`, so a change there fires on both the derive and the composer.
recommendations: Q1 -- WHERE THE CHECK LIVES AND HOW IT DEGRADES. Put it in `_otr_ledger_freeze.run_gap_audit` as a new `_check_gNN_*(ledger_data, errors, warnings)` that appends to `warnings` ONLY, plus a test-side mirror. G14's own history is both the precedent and the argument: `_check_g14_provenance_publish` used to append to `errors`, which at Phase 10 raises `FreezeAssertionError` and destroyed a finished render; it was moved to `warnings` on 2026-08-15 for exactly the reason THE LAW states. `tests/test_cross_play_frame_leak.py` states the same rule in its own docstring ('a test/receipt assertion, never a runtime reject. Nothing in this file is imported by the generation path'). Degrade path = append a string to a list. obs volume is untouched by construction: the check writes no verdict any consumer gates on. No retry ladder -- the anchor is right that `CastingFailedError` on ladder exhaustion is the precedent for a check that reduces output.

Q1 -- WHAT IS COMPARED, AND WHY NOT THE IDEA ON RECORD. Do not build 'names the ledger work_title OR names no work'. It false-positives and false-negatives on the same corpus: 'the salt-sprayed deck of the Pequod' names no work and passes only by accident, while a correct line like 'from Melville's great whaling novel' names a work and fails. `tests/test_cross_play_frame_leak.py` already documents two measured designs that were rejected for exactly this (one 'returns mostly legitimate relational prose', the other 'REJECTS THE CORRECT SETTING on five of the fourteen manifest rows'), and the surviving design is the INVERSION. Take the same inversion here: once the work name is template-rendered, assert only that the row contains no SECOND title-shaped span -- a quoted/italicized span, or a 'The Adventure/Case/Mystery/Tale of X' pattern -- that is not the rendered work label or the rendered subtitle. That predicate has a small, enumerable false-positive surface (an in-world quoted object, 'the file marked Blackwood'), which is survivable because the output is a warning an operator reads.

Q1 -- NORMALIZATION, EXACTLY. For the one comparison that is needed: `str.strip()` -> `unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', ...)` (match `_otr_bark_lib`'s own transform so the check sees what TTS will say) -> `casefold()` (the repo's existing idiom in `_otr_continuity`, `_otr_ledger_clean`, `_otr_ledger`) -> collapse internal whitespace -> drop a leading 'the '/'a '/'an ' -> strip ASCII and curly quotes and trailing punctuation. Do NOT normalize act numerals: compare against the string the TEMPLATE ACTUALLY EMITTED, never a re-derivation. A checker that re-derives what the renderer rendered is the producer/consumer literal split that `PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG` exists to prevent (BUG_BIBLE 12.86, cited in `_otr_ledger_clean`). On media_archive the check returns early on the `ADAPTATION_SOURCE_KINDS` gate -- inert, not 'check the publication instead'.

Q2 -- THE TEMPERATURE ANSWER, VERIFIED, AND IT IS A LEVER THE ANCHOR NEVER MEASURED. The announcer call runs at `_otr_line_composer._BASE_TEMPERATURE = 0.8`, passed explicitly by `_announcer_generate` from `_authored_or_one_more_ask`. The writer's `creativity` widget (`_CREATIVITY_TEMP_MAP`, balanced 0.85) does NOT reach this path -- only `top_p`/`min_p`/`repetition_penalty` do, closure-captured through `_SlotScheduler.sampling` into `_build_truncating_generate_fn`, which sets `do_sample=True` unconditionally. The cool path already exists (`_STRUCTURAL_RETRY_TEMPERATURE = 0.35`) but `_authored_or_one_more_ask` reaches it only when `validate_announcer_line` fails, and that validator checks ONLY non-empty and absence of `[]{}`. A semantically wrong line is structurally perfect, so the cool retry is unreachable for this defect class by construction. Temperature is not an alternative to the register hypothesis; it is the sampler that lets whichever attractor is strongest win, and lowering it on the intro is a cheap, testable intervention nobody has tried.

Q2 -- THE INSTRUCTION-ATTRACTOR ANSWER. 'we gather for' appears in no pack and no Python prompt (grepped `nodes/` and `config/`) -- that phrasing is the model's own. But the live pack seam carries a naming imperative, 'Sentence 1 names tonight's work from the WORK line', and the WORK line rendered `a scene from Nonsense Novels`. Told to name a work, holding a CONTAINER title, having just been handed a one-sentence summary of a detective scene, naming the container is the least likely completion. Note the near-miss that reframes the whole bug: the real piece title IS 'Maddened by Mystery, or The Defective Detective' and it sits in `source_meta.unit_label` on this very ledger -- the fact the model needed was on disk and deliberately withheld from the prompt by `identity_from_meta`'s no-unit_label rule. That is a better-supported mechanism than 'bland title loses' and it is checkable against ledgers rather than against a re-run.

Q2 -- VERDICT ON THE HYPOTHESIS. Not broken, but not established, and it is not the only live explanation. Three routes survive: named-entity transport through the ungated `opening_status_quo`, a hot free sample with no semantic validator, and a seam that orders a work to be named while the WORK value is a container. The anchor closed the round; it should be reopened as one cheap measurement -- re-run the same lane and stamp the derive output in `meta`, which nothing does today.

Q3 -- COMMIT: YES, BUT NOT THE VALIDATOR ON RECORD. Against a validator: once the name is template-rendered the fidelity fact is un-inventable, and `_otr_ledger_clean`'s own docstring argues the repo's standing preference -- 'the protected text must be physically unable to enter the model's edit surface ... a post-hoc "did the fact survive" check ships the wrong row and merely notices.' For a validator: the residual is not 'the model names the wrong work', it is 'a LATER PASS deletes the rendered name', and that has already happened once, measured, on the sibling surface (PBUG-20260815-01, 9 of 14 voiced rows). So build a RECEIPT check, not a prose check: assert the Python-rendered work label is still present in the final intro row after `ledger_clean`, normalized as above. It compares a string Python rendered against a row Python wrote -- zero paraphrase surface, zero false positives by construction. The title-shaped-span check is the second, softer layer and stays a warning.

Q3 -- THE STRUCTURAL HALF IS A GENUINE r2 FORK, NOT A LOOKUP. Stamping the intro row with `PROTECTED_FACT_COMPONENT_FLAG` works but that flag is documented as a WHOLE-ROW skip, and the intro row is mostly model prose that legitimately needs cleaning -- whole-row protection would silently exempt the intro from the clean pass. Three defensible answers: (a) a narrower flag that names the protected SPAN rather than the row; (b) accept whole-row protection and lose intro cleaning; (c) re-render the deterministic half AFTER `ledger_clean` so Python asserts the label last. (c) is cheapest, keeps cleaning, and makes the receipt check trivially true. This is exactly the 'more than one defensible answer' test in the operator's 08-17 amendment -- it earns the arc.

Q4 -- WHERE THE DEDUPE LIVES: NOWHERE TODAY, AND ITS HOME IS A DECISION. There is no unit_label/title comparison anywhere in the repo, because `_otr_source_identity.identity_from_meta` never reads `unit_label` ('`unit_label` is deliberately NOT read -- see the module docstring'). Put the new `locator` on `SourceIdentity` as a field plus its `provenance` entry, deduped at extraction: it is the declared single bibliographic authority, `SourceIdentity.as_receipt` already carries `field_provenance` so a wrong locator is fixable at its source, and `compose_announcer_intro`'s own comment states the split -- 'the field owns the fact, the composer owns the phrasing'. Putting it in `_otr_line_composer._work_line` forks the authority and gives the coda and the announcer two different ideas of one work.

Q4 -- WHAT ACTUALLY COLLIDES, MEASURED. Exact casefolded collisions in the 65-unit manifest are 5: The Stolen White Elephant, The Canterville Ghost, Pigs Is Pigs, Told After Supper, and The Secret Sharer. The Secret Sharer is the one that matters -- title 'The Secret Sharer' vs label 'The secret sharer' -- so a case-SENSITIVE `==` misses it and ships the stutter. Equality is also not enough: 'Green Tea; Mr. Justice Harbottle' / 'Green Tea' is a prefix collision, and four sources carry multiple units ('The Wonderful Wizard of Oz' x3, 'Nonsense Novels' x2, 'A Christmas Garland' x2, 'Sketches New and Old' x2). Use containment in EITHER direction after casefold + whitespace-collapse + leading-article strip, not equality.

Q4 -- THE SUBTITLE AXIS IS A DIFFERENT PROBLEM. 'The Blackwood Enigma: The Blackwood Enigma' cannot arise on an adaptation lane, because the left half is the work and the right half is `meta['episode_title']` and those differ by construction. The two real subtitle hazards are: (a) an LLM episode title that already contains the work name ('Macbeth: A Scene from Macbeth'), which the same containment dedupe catches; and (b) `episode_title` carrying a harness run label, which NO dedupe can catch -- gate that branch on `meta['title_source']` and refuse a planted/user value, reusing `scripts/otr_gpu_soak_matrix.HEADLESS_FORBIDDEN_TITLE_SOURCE`'s reasoning rather than re-deriving it.
must_fix: Do not render public_domain `unit_label` as a spoken locator unqualified. ~half of the 60 differing labels in `config/source_banks/public_domain_story/manifest.sample.json` are curator scene descriptors, not locators that exist in the work; speaking them makes the deterministic half invent on the invent-nothing lane. Either add an explicit per-unit piece-title flag to the manifest (a data change, operator-visible), or restrict the locator half to shakespeare `act`+`scene` and to units whose label is demonstrably a piece title, falling through to the subtitle shape otherwise.

Do not render shakespeare `scene_label`; it is a compound carrying a curator descriptor after a dash ('Act 1, Scene 2 - Prospero opens the island's history'). Build the locator from the `act` and `scene` INTS emitted by `_otr_shakespeare_sources.source_meta_from_scene`, and decide numeral rendering deliberately (no int-to-roman helper exists in the repo).

Protect the rendered work label from `_otr_ledger_clean`, or re-render it after the clean pass. Unprotected, PBUG-20260815-01 replays on the intro.

Correct the seam citation before r2. `_otr_line_composer._ANNOUNCER_INTRO_SYSTEM_SAFE` is the science-lane extraction fixture; the live seam is `nodes/story_packs/public_domain/faithful_radio_adaptation.json` key `announcer_intro_safe_system`, reached via `_otr_creative_prompt_router.resolve_creative_system_prompt` -> `_otr_story_pack.get_pack_prompt` (which raises rather than falling back). Any prompt-side proposal aimed at the constant edits dead text.

A validator read written from this anchor must read `meta['announcer_intro_rewrite']['status']`, not `meta['announcer_intro_rewrite']` -- the field is a dict with `status` and `reason`.
